evidence: TaskController.router() only maps HTTP routes (POST /users, POST /projects, POST/GET /projects/:projectId/tasks, PATCH /tasks/:taskId/done) to TaskManagementService methods.
text() and parameter() check only the types and shapes of transport input (string vs non-string, single vs array route parameter), not business rules.
Task status parsing is delegated to the domain function asTaskStatus instead of being reimplemented in the controller.
handle() wraps actions with HTTP status codes and JSON serialization and forwards errors through next(error), which is a pure transport concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is an Express HTTP controller that sits in the infrastructure layer. Its responsibilities are transport concerns: it registers routes, checks the shapes of request bodies, route parameters and query parameters, maps HTTP status codes and serializes JSON responses, and passes errors to Express middleware. That fits an infrastructure/adapter role. Every business operation (creating users, projects and tasks, listing tasks, marking a task done) is delegated to TaskManagementService. Status values are converted by the domain's asTaskStatus rather than by rules written in the controller. The text() and parameter() helpers only check data types at the transport boundary, not business rules. No persistence or domain logic is embedded here.
